items.title: What is a pre-launch or coming soon landing page?
items.description: A page published before the product is available. It explains what is coming and collects email addresses from people who want to know when it does. Its success metric is signups, not sales.

items.title: What should I offer in exchange for the email?
items.description: Something only an early signup gets: early access, a launch price, a say in the roadmap. The reason to sign up today rather than after launch is the whole conversion argument of the page, so state it next to the form.

items.title: Do I need a countdown?
items.description: Only if the date will not move. A visible date beats a vague “coming soon”: it tells visitors how long they are being asked to wait and gives the emails a natural rhythm. Without one, state an honest window and let the roadmap make it concrete.

items.title: How much of the product should I show?
items.description: One real thing: a screen, a clip, a draft, labelled work in progress if it is. And nothing you cannot ship: promise zero features you cannot show.

items.title: What do I send to the people who signed up?
items.description: What the page promised, when it promised it: short progress emails (what shipped, what changed, one behind-the-scenes image), then the early-access link and the launch price. Showing the subject lines before the signup is what keeps unsubscribes low.
